add.issue.name: Track llama-swap models as GPU claims

edit.description.md:
The AI plane only knows Ollama. A llama-swap server on the same machine loads models the Resource Engine can't name: each llama-server process shows up as an anonymous GPU process, with no passport in Flow and no way to ask it to unload.

Scope:
- Add a llama-swap host setting next to the Ollama host.
- Read the running models from llama-swap's `/running` endpoint on the existing AI poll pattern (5s while reachable, 30s while not). Poll nothing when no host is set.
- Each running model becomes a `gpu-vram` claim and a workload passport, owner `llama-swap`. VRAM comes from the measured nvidia-smi figure for its llama-server PID (via `GpuVramSource.adopt`), so it isn't counted twice.
- A graceful stop unloads the model through `POST /api/models/unload/:id`, and the receipt settles once the next poll proves the model is gone.

Out of scope: shell shelter or slimming when a model loads. That comes next, built on these claims.

Decided to poll `/running` rather than subscribe to `/api/events`, because the event stream also carries every upstream log line (about 165 KB during one load).

kdeconnectd relies on D-Bus activation, which did not fire: the tray indicator ran with no daemon behind it, port 1716 had no listener, and phone pairing failed both by discovery and by IP.

Fix: start kdeconnectd as a supervised user unit (Restart=on-failure) plus the tray indicator from startup.lua.

add.issue.name: Installer: detect every NVIDIA driver, and skip nvidia-open on pre-Turing cards

edit.description.md:
GitHub #209 reports "Install package failed: nvidia-open-dkms" with no log. Review found two ways the installer produces that failure or worse:

1. Driver detection matches package names (`nvidia`, `nvidia-open`, their `-lts`/`-dkms` variants). Legacy branches (`nvidia-580xx-dkms`), beta drivers and distro kernel-module packages (`linux-cachyos-nvidia-open`) slip through, so the keep/replace prompt never shows. The installer then installs `nvidia-open-dkms`, which conflicts with the installed `NVIDIA-MODULE`, and `--noconfirm` refuses the removal.
2. Arch's repos carry only the open kernel modules now, and those need Turing or newer. On a Pascal, Maxwell or older card with no driver, the installer puts on a driver that cannot run the GPU.

Fix: detect by `Provides: NVIDIA-MODULE`. Treat a requirement as installed when any installed package satisfies it (`pacman -T`), so `nvidia-580xx-utils` covers `nvidia-utils`. On pre-Turing GPUs keep whatever driver exists or skip the driver with the exact legacy-branch command, and skip the mkinitcpio module wiring when no driver module is installed.

- Every owner with a shelter hook is asked to shelter. Plugins that declare `shelter = "unload"` drop their surfaces until exit.
- Flow shows an "Inference mode" passport. Settings > AI gets an Auto/Off switch with live tok/s.
- `qs ipc call inference enter|exit|auto|off|status`.

add.issue.name: PRIORITY: project knowledge that stays current and fits a small context

edit.description.md:
The project's working notes (vision, decisions, status, ledger, playbooks, known issues) are spread across many long markdown files. Two problems follow:
- They go stale, because updates depend on each session remembering. A tracked-file claim, a dev VM address and an open-PR list were all wrong in one week.
- Local models with small contexts choke reading them, and even large-context agents spend their first minutes re-verifying.

Goal: nothing gets lost, every agent (local or remote) retrieves only what it needs, and facts refresh from the source of truth instead of from memory.

Plan:
1. **Generated index.** A command builds one compact catalog: each note's title, one-line purpose, and every heading with its line range and last-verified date. Agents read the index (a few KB), then open one section by line range.
2. **Facts checked, not remembered.** A checker verifies machine-checkable claims in the notes: PR numbers and their state, branches, tracked files, reachable hosts, versions. It flags stale sections with the evidence. It runs on every PR in CI, after a merge from a git hook, and at session start.
3. **Status generated.** The "in flight" view is built from open PRs and this board, not written by hand.
4. **One write path.** A `note` command appends dated entries in the right place, so a session never edits a long file by hand.
5. **Small-context retrieval.** One query command returns the top few matching sections under a token budget, served over CLI and MCP so local models and remote agents use the same path. It builds on the semantic index already running on this machine.

Done when a local model with a 16k context can answer "what is in flight and why" from a single query, and a merged PR updates status with no human step.

add.issue.name: Performance budget with a regression check

edit.description.md:
Measured 2026-09-22 on an RTX 4090 with two 3440x1440 monitors: the idle desktop holds about 913 MiB of VRAM (quickshell 318, Hyprland 168), and Hyprland uses 7-13% SM at idle. Nothing catches a regression, and 8.4 points of idle GPU (PERF-01) are still unattributed.

- An `aphotic perf snapshot` command records per-process VRAM and SM, idle renders per second, and RSS. It writes a dated row and diffs against the last one.
- Attribute quickshell's 318 MiB: per-screen textures, layer caches, wallpaper decode.
- Set the budget: under 500 MiB shell VRAM while inference mode is active. Fail loudly when a change breaks it.

add.issue.name: One adapter contract for local inference backends

edit.description.md:
`LlamaSwapClaims` is largely a copy of `OllamaClaims`. `GpuVramSource` special-cases Ollama, and `AiProviders` carries a separate poll per backend. ComfyUI and Kokoro would be the third and fourth copies.

Define one backend contract: list running models with memory, map models to PIDs, unload a model, report stats. One claimant then turns any backend into claims, passports and receipts. Ollama and llama-swap become the first two adapters, with behavior unchanged and covered by the existing tests.

add.issue.name: One wallpaper renderer: the shell's background window, not awww too

edit.description.md:
Each wallpaper change reaches two renderers. awww-daemon paints it on its own background-layer surface, and the shell's opaque background window paints it again on top, so awww's copy is never seen. Measured 2026-09-23 on two 3440x1440 screens:
- awww-daemon itself: 2 MiB RSS and no GPU memory.
- The real cost is the compositor's texture for the hidden surface, about 19 MiB per screen showing an image.

The oversized decode fix (#221) is the much bigger win. This ticket removes the remaining duplicate.

The maintainer chose the shell's background window as the owner. Steps:
1. Make `~/.config/awww/current-wallpaper` the single source of truth for "what is shown". Replace `awww query` in the sddm and greeter sync.
2. Have the theme CLI, first-boot apply and the wallpaper scripts set the wallpaper through that file or the shell's IPC, not `awww img`.
3. Start awww-daemon only when the background window is disabled, as a fallback.

add.issue.name: Inference mode for any local model host, on any GPU

edit.description.md:
Inference mode keys on what a runtime reports, not on model names or one backend:
- A `LocalInference` registry gathers each backend adapter's loaded models, each with an embedding flag the runtime provides: llama-swap from launch flags, Ollama from `/api/show` capabilities, LM Studio from the model `type`.
- The mode enters when any backend has a loaded chat model, or a measured claim of 2 GiB or more.
- A new LM Studio adapter joins Ollama and llama-swap.
- The trigger doesn't depend on NVIDIA measurement, so an RTX 3070, a 4090 or a non-NVIDIA card get the same behavior.
- No model names or naming conventions appear in code.

add.issue.name: Will it fit? Show which local models fit the GPU right now

edit.description.md: Linux has no VRAM spill to system RAM: a model that doesn't fit fails to load. The shell already measures what the desktop and every loaded model hold. Use that to show, per configured model (read from the backend, never hard-coded), whether it fits in the VRAM free right now. Surface it in the AI notch tab and Settings > AI. It works on any card size, so an 8 GB RTX 3070 user sees the same answer shape as a 24 GB 4090 user.

add.issue.name: Chat with your local models from the shell

edit.description.md: llama-swap and LM Studio speak the OpenAI API. Add them as chat providers in the AI chat and Intelligence panel, with the model list read from the backend. A user who serves models locally then talks to them from the desktop with no cloud account. Inference mode and the claims already follow those models.

add.issue.name: A game and a loaded model share the GPU cleanly

edit.description.md: Starting a game while a model is loaded should raise one clear prompt: suspend the model (unload it through its backend) or keep both. When the game ends the model loads again on the next request. Verify end to end with GameMode and a real game on NVIDIA and AMD. Inference mode and the Gaming profile must not fight over shelter or render settings when both are active.

add.issue.name: Security engagements and local models in Flow and the audit

edit.description.md: Security engagements already claim CPU and memory. They should keep running through inference mode (inference pauses effects and opt-out plugins, never a user's work). Tool runs that call a local model through a harness should show the model in the agent audit, so an engagement log records which local model answered.

add.issue.name: Bar: stop forking hyprctl every 2 seconds for keyboard state

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** The bar reads caps lock, num lock and the keyboard layout by running `hyprctl -j devices` on a 2 s timer, forever. Measured on an idle desktop: 22 to 30 hyprctl processes a minute, the largest share of the shell's idle process spawns.

**Plan.** The layout already arrives on Hyprland's `activelayout` event. Caps and num lock come from the kernel's keyboard LED files under `/sys/class/leds/*::capslock` and `*::numlock`, read in-process with `FileView` (no fork). Hyprland mirrors lock state to every keyboard's LEDs, so any LED that reads on means the lock is on. Machines with no keyboard LEDs (VMs, some virtual keyboards) keep the old hyprctl poll as a fallback.

**Done when.** Idle hyprctl spawns drop to zero on a machine with keyboard LEDs, and the lock icons and layout still update.

add.issue.name: SystemUsage: read /proc/stat and /proc/meminfo in process, not with head and cat

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** `services/SystemUsage.qml` runs `head -n1 /proc/stat` and `cat /proc/meminfo` on a 2 s timer that is always on. That is 60 process spawns a minute at idle, the most of any poller in the shell, to read two small kernel files.

**Plan.** Read both files with `FileView` and `reload()` on the same tick, the way `NetworkUsage.qml` already reads `/proc/net/dev`. Keep the parsing. Then gate the timer on a real consumer being visible (the bar's resource indicator, dashboard, notch), like `ShellUsage.qml`'s holder count.

**Done when.** Zero child processes from this service at idle, CPU and memory readings unchanged.

add.issue.name: Shell RAM sits at 385 to 495 MB against a 350 MB budget

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** The idle shell measured 495 MB RSS, then 385 MB a few minutes later (Pss 338 MB, 300 MB of it private dirty anonymous memory, mostly JS and QML heap). The budget for a base install is 350 MB. Nobody has attributed where it goes.

**Plan.** Attribute before cutting. Take RSS and JS heap at start, after opening each surface once, and after closing them all, to find what stays resident after its surface closes. Check the largest singletons and model caches (launcher apps, emoji list, clipboard history, wallpaper thumbnails). Write the numbers down with the method used.

**Done when.** A per-surface table of resident cost exists and the top two holders have tickets.

add.issue.name: AI hosts: poll Ollama, LM Studio and llama-swap over HTTP in process, not by forking curl

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** `services/ai/AiProviders.qml` forks `curl` to poll Ollama's `/api/ps` every 5 s while Ollama answers, even with no model loaded (12 spawns a minute measured). LM Studio has the same poll, and llama-swap's `/running` also polls every 30 s next to its event stream.

**Plan.** Use QML's built-in `XMLHttpRequest` for these short JSON GETs, so no process starts. Keep the intervals and the back-off. Leave the long-lived llama-swap event stream on its own ticket.

**Done when.** No curl child processes from these polls, same models and claims reported.

add.issue.name: llama-swap event stream pipes every server log line into the shell during inference

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** The shell holds `curl -sN /api/events` open to catch model load and unload. That stream also carries every upstream log line and in-flight counter. Measured during one agent run: 304 KB in 20 s, about 25 lines a second, each one a JavaScript call in the shell, when only `modelStatus` events are used. The cost lands while a model is generating, when the machine is busiest.

**Plan.** Filter before the shell sees the line: check whether llama-swap can subscribe to model status only; if not, pipe through `grep --line-buffered '"type":"modelStatus"'` so JavaScript sees only the events it acts on.

**Done when.** A generation run sends only model status lines to the shell, and load and unload still update within a second.

add.issue.name: Theme state and palette files are re-read every second forever

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** `services/Themes.qml` and `services/Colours.qml` each reload a file on a 1 s timer, because the file watch stops firing after the CLI or wallust replaces the file with an atomic rename. That is two wakeups a second, forever, to catch a change that happens a few times a day.

**Plan.** Re-arm the watch when it fires (reset `path` after a change so a fresh watch lands on the new file), or watch the parent directory for the rename. Keep a slow poll (30 s or more) only as a safety net if the re-armed watch proves unreliable.

**Done when.** Repeated `aphotic theme set` and `aphotic wallpaper -f` in one session update the shell each time, and the 1 s timers are gone.

add.issue.name: Lock screen polls its own lock state every 500 ms while unlocked

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** `modules/lock/Lock.qml` copies `lock.locked` into `SessionLockState` on a 500 ms timer that always runs, because the change signal did not fire reliably. Two wakeups a second, all day, to feed the wallpaper auto-cycle pause.

**Plan.** Set `SessionLockState.locked` at the places the shell itself locks and unlocks (the lock IPC, idle lock, and the Pam success handler), and keep a slow poll only if some lock path the shell does not own exists.

**Done when.** No sub-second timer runs while unlocked, and the wallpaper cycle still pauses on lock.

add.issue.name: HostInfo forks ip route every 15 s while nmcli monitor already reports changes

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** `services/HostInfo.qml` runs `ip route get 1.1.1.1` every 15 s to show the local IP. The shell already keeps `nmcli monitor` open, which reports every connection change. `services/AgentProviders.qml` also runs three `pgrep` calls a minute when no harness hook is sending events.

**Plan.** Refresh the IP when `Nmcli` reports a change, plus once at start. For the pgrep fallback, stop it once any harness hook has sent an event this session (partly done) and read `/proc` in process instead of forking pgrep.

**Done when.** No periodic `ip` or `pgrep` spawns at idle on a machine with hooks installed.

add.issue.comment.md: Lead from the boot-path review: several surfaces that are closed at idle appear to be built at start and construct their singletons with them. Settings (its Appearance pane pulls in `Themes` and its 1 s poll), the launcher (`LauncherUsage`, `PinnedSnippets`), the package installer (`PkgSearch`), the notification center (`Weather`), the keybind cheatsheet (`HyprKeybinds`, which runs `hyprctl binds` at start) and the wallpaper picker model. Check each against a `Loader { active: open }` pattern first; this is the likeliest place the resident memory goes.
add.issue.comment.author: 82D6ZVRHW7Q89JK5Z846NWXBMY

add.issue.name: Install: nightly canary that installs every base package for real

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** CI runs the installer as a dry run on pull requests only. When an upstream Arch or AUR package breaks (an AUR wayland build, an nvidia package), nobody on the project knows until a user fails to install and reports it.

**Plan.** A scheduled workflow in `archlinux:latest` that runs nightly: resolve and install every package in both base profiles, build the AUR ones, and record the exact version set on success (`known-good.lock`, date-stamped). On failure, open or update one issue per broken package. Publish `status.json` (last green date, broken packages) on the Pages site for the installer and `aphotic doctor` to read.

**Done when.** A deliberately missing package turns the canary red, opens one issue, and a later green run closes it.

add.issue.name: Install: plain-language failures and a one-step, opt-in GitHub report

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** When a package fails, the user sees pacman or AUR helper output and a log path. Most people give up there, and we never hear about it.

**Plan.** On any failure: name the package and the likely cause in one sentence, offer the automatic fallback (snapshot retry, once it exists), then offer to report. Build a redacted bundle (install log tail, profile, GPU vendor, package versions; no usernames, hostnames or paths under home), show it, and on yes open a prefilled issue URL, or run `gh issue create` when `gh` is signed in. Title the issue `install: <package> failed (<date>)` so reports group onto the canary's issue. Nothing is sent without a yes.

**Done when.** A forced failure on the dev VM ends in one prompt that produces a correct, redacted issue.

add.issue.name: Install: default to the latest release tag, with an edge channel for main

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** New users clone and install `main`, so a regression merged at noon reaches everyone installing that afternoon.

**Plan.** The installer and the README one-liner check out the newest release tag by default. `--channel edge` keeps `main` for testers. Each release carries the `known-good.lock` its canary passed with. `aphotic update` follows the channel the user chose.

**Done when.** A fresh install lands on the latest tag, and `--channel edge` lands on `main`.

add.issue.name: Install: fall back to the last known-good Arch snapshot when a package is broken

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** When a current package is broken upstream, the install stops and the user has no way forward.

**Plan.** When a package fails, retry it from the Arch Linux Archive at the canary's last green date. A leaf package (nothing depends on it) is installed from the archive and held with a temporary `IgnorePkg`. A core library (wayland, mesa, nvidia) switches the whole transaction to that day's archive snapshot, because Arch does not support a partial upgrade. `aphotic doctor` lifts the hold and returns to live mirrors once the canary is green again. Every step is shown and reversible.

**Depends on** the nightly canary's lock and status file.

**Done when.** On the dev VM, a package forced to fail installs from the snapshot and the desktop comes up.

add.issue.name: Install: signed Aphotic pacman repo so no user compiles AUR packages

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** Eight base packages come from the AUR and build on the user's machine: swaylock-effects, zsh-theme-powerlevel10k-git, oh-my-zsh-git, papirus-folders, bibata-cursor-theme, python-pyamdgpuinfo, python-pywalfox, visual-studio-code-bin. Any one of them, or the AUR helper bootstrap, can break an install.

**Plan.** CI builds these into a signed pacman repo published on GitHub Releases, rebuilt when the canary is green. The installer adds `[aphotic]` and installs binaries. Move `visual-studio-code-bin` from base into the dev plane. Keep the AUR path only as a fallback.

**Done when.** A base install on a clean VM uses no AUR helper at all.

add.issue.name: Install: offline installer ISO built from the last known-good snapshot

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** Even with snapshot fallback, an install needs working mirrors and network.

**Plan.** An archiso image built monthly by CI from the last green snapshot, with an offline cache of every base package, so Aphotic installs with no upstream at all. Must fit the 2 GiB release asset limit. Starts after the snapshot fallback and binary repo exist, so the ISO reuses them instead of becoming a second, untested install path.

**Done when.** The ISO installs to a working desktop on a VM with networking off.

add.issue.name: Settings: UI polish pass with current Qt 6 techniques

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** The settings menu works but does not yet feel like the rest of the shell at its best: transitions, density, focus handling and scrolling vary from pane to pane.

**Plan.** Audit every pane against the Qt 6.11 docs (not memory): `Qt Quick` states and transitions, `Behavior` on layout changes, `ListView` section headers and reuse (`reuseItems`), keyboard focus chains (`KeyNavigation`, `FocusScope`), `TextMetrics` for alignment, and `layer` only where it pays. Keep the shared flyout chrome. Pair every wheel scroll with a draggable scrollbar. Measure open time and renders per pane before and after.

**Done when.** Every pane passes a consistency checklist, and no pane opens slower or renders more than before.

add.issue.name: Bar: polish and performance pass across all five bar styles

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** The five bar styles grew one at a time. They differ in spacing, hover and popout behavior, and idle cost, and nobody has measured them side by side.

**Plan.** For each style, measure idle renders per 10 s and RSS with the method in the performance baseline. Then align the shared parts (spacing tokens, hover, popout anchoring, animation curves) using the Qt 6.11 docs as the reference, and cut any per-style idle animation or binding that repaints. Record the numbers per style.

**Done when.** All five styles meet the idle render budget and share one component set for the parts they have in common.

add.issue.name: Live window peek previews when no model is loaded

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** Window switching and the dock show icons and titles, not what is on screen. The shell already uses `ScreencopyView` for the area and color pickers, but not for previews.

**Plan.** Live previews of open windows in the dock hover, the switcher and workspace overviews, using `ScreencopyView` with `live` capture only while the preview is visible and a low capture rate. Previews run freely when no local model is loaded. When inference mode takes the GPU, they drop to a static last frame or an icon and come back when the model unloads, as the inference-mode decision already requires. Measure GPU and VRAM cost per visible preview.

**Done when.** Hovering the dock shows a live preview, previews cost nothing when hidden, and loading a model turns them static.

add.issue.name: Model library plugin: installed models, similar models on Hugging Face, and fit-based suggestions

edit.description.md:

**Plan.** A workspace plugin with three views. Installed: the llama-swap roster and GGUF files on disk, with size, quant and VRAM fit. Similar: a cached list of Hugging Face models that match the installed ones in quant and style (architecture, dense or MoE, draft head, vision). Suggested: when nothing similar matches, run `llmfit` to rank new quants that fit this GPU's VRAM budget. Uses the same VRAM math as the Resource Engine. Everything works offline from the cache.

**Done when.** The plugin lists this machine's installed models correctly and offers at least one fitting suggestion.

add.issue.name: Harness hooks v2: one event and stats contract for every agent harness

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** Claude Code reports rich state to the shell (session events, token usage, quota, model). Other harnesses report little or nothing, and OpenCode's hooks predate the current format.

**Plan.** Write down one harness-neutral contract: session start and end, turn, tool call, model id, token counts, cost when known, quota when known. Every harness adapter emits it into the existing agent events stream. Agent audit and the agent graph read only the contract, so every harness registers with its model id the way Claude does now.

**Done when.** The contract is documented, Claude's hook emits it, and agent audit and the graph render a second harness from it with no harness-specific code.

**Done when.** A Pi session shows up in the graph and audit with the right model and token counts.

edit.description.md:
**Plan.** A `harness-hook` plugin for Empryo that emits the v2 hook contract from its `--json` usage and session output (token counts are real as of 2026-09-23). Registers in agent audit and the agent graph with its model id.

**Done when.** An Empryo session shows up in the graph and audit with the right model and token counts.

**Done when.** An OpenCode session shows the same fields in the graph and audit as a Claude session.

add.issue.name: Harness hook: upgrade Codex's hook to the v2 contract

edit.description.md:

**Plan.** A `harness-hook` plugin for dsh that emits the v2 contract. First step: find what dsh exposes (hooks, session files, JSON output) and note the gaps on this ticket. Registers in agent audit and the agent graph with its model id.

add.issue.name: Install fails on plain Arch: yay's build output ends up in the AUR helper name

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** On a machine without yay (any plain Arch install), the installer builds yay and captures `ensure_aur_helper`'s stdout as the helper name. `install_yay` printed the whole build to stdout, so `AUR_HELPER` held the build log plus `yay`, and the first package install failed with `yay: File name too long`. Found by a real install of v2.0.5 on a fresh Arch VM: it stopped at `qt5-wayland`, the first package. `main` has the same code. The nightly canary missed it because it bootstraps yay itself instead of running `install.sh`.

**Plan.** Send the yay clone and build output to stderr, and keep only a helper name that resolves as a command in `install.sh`.

**Done when.** A full install on a fresh Arch VM with no yay finishes.

add.issue.name: Non-interactive install leaves bare Hyprland: config copy defaults to no

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** With no options and no terminal (a piped or scripted install), the installer promises the zero-prompt daily-driver setup, but the config-copy prompt still runs with its default of no. The install finishes with `Configs copied: no`: Hyprland with none of Aphotic's desktop. Found on a fresh Arch VM.

**Plan.** On that daily-driver default path, when stdin is not a terminal and nobody chose, copy the configs. Interactive runs still ask, and re-runs that reuse an existing config are unchanged, so customized configs are never overwritten silently.

**Done when.** A fresh non-interactive install reports `Configs copied: yes`.
